target.name: runtime-installed IWRAM Q10 fixed-point transforms
target.role: Q10 fixed-point transforms: a twelve-term sum of products over three lanes (0x087B7F04) and a three-term dot product (0x087B80A4), both accumulating signed 32x32 products into 64 bits and reducing with `lsr #10` / `add ..., lsl #22`
target.notes: THE THIRD BATCH OF THE SAME RUNTIME-INSTALLED BLOCK. The 4100 bytes at ROM 0x087B79A4..0x087B89A8 are the image of IWRAM 0x03000000..0x03001004, installed by the reset code's second DMA3 program (SAD 0x087B79A4, DAD 0x03000000, CNT 0x84000401 = 1025 words), so IWRAM X = ROM 0x087B79A4 + (X - 0x03000000) and every byte is statically known. The block's code half ends at 0x03000F44; this batch covers the byte-lane and Q-format transform families inside it. TWO ADJACENT ROUTINES IN ONE UNIT, and the adjacency is the evidence: 0x087B7F04 (IWRAM 0x03000560) is 416 bytes and 104 instructions ending at the `bx lr` at IWRAM 0x030006FC, and 0x087B80A4 (IWRAM 0x03000700) begins at exactly that next address, 104 bytes and 26 instructions ending at the `bx lr` at IWRAM 0x03000764. Neither has a pc-relative load, so neither has a pool. THE SHARED ELEMENT IS THE REDUCTION, and getting its exact contract right took three attempts. `lsr rD, RO, #10` followed by `add rD, rD, RH, lsl #22` computes, for every 64-bit pattern, exactly `(u32)(((u64)sum) >> 10)`: the high word contributes its low 22 bits at result bits 22..43 of which 32..43 are truncated, and bits 10..31 of the low word land at result bits 0..21. That is an identity, not an approximation. It is ALSO identical to an ARITHMETIC shift truncated the same way, `(u32)(((s64)sum) >> 10)`, because an `asr` differs from an `lsr` only in the bits it shifts in at the top and after truncation to 32 bits those are all above bit 31. THIS TICKET ASSERTED A DIFFERENCE THREE TIMES AND WAS WRONG EACH TIME; the source comment claiming `lsr` was load-bearing was wrong and has been corrected, because a wrong reason is as bad as a wrong value. The ten discarded bits ARE discarded: there is no rounding term and no saturation instruction anywhere in either routine. THE REDUCTION APPEARS IN TWO SPELLINGS and both must be recognised: the STANDALONE form `lsr rD,RO,#10` + `add rD,rD,RH,lsl #22`, and the FOLDED form `add rD,ACC,RO,lsr #10` + `add rD,rD,RH,lsl #22`. 0x087B80A4 uses the folded form three times; 0x087B7F04 uses the standalone form nine times and the folded form ONCE, for its last group - so a pattern scan keyed on the folded form alone finds 3 of its 12 reductions and under-counts the family by 9. THE TWO ROUTINES ARE NOT THE SAME OPERATION, which is the question this ticket exists to settle. 0x087B80A4 reduces ONCE per output word after all three products, so its intermediate is a genuine 64-bit sum and cannot wrap. 0x087B7F04 reduces EACH LANE SEPARATELY and then adds the three reduced 32-bit values into one accumulator per lane, with 32-bit wraparound - a different computation, not a rearrangement, because the bits discarded from one product cannot carry into another. The test measures that difference on a case chosen to show it (a case with equal coefficients does NOT show it, because multiplying by three commutes with the shift), and also measures that the third lane of 0x087B7F04's last group folds its `lsr` into the accumulator in place of a zero. WHO CALLS THEM: the Thumb-to-ARM veneers at 0x08049174 and 0x08049180, each with exactly ONE Thumb BL caller in the image, at 0x0802EFD0 and 0x0802F1DC. Neither call site resolves all four register arguments inside a readable window, so the register roles come from the routines' own instructions and not from the call sites - stated rather than glossed over. THE SCALE: the shift discards ten fraction bits, so the arithmetic is Q10 IF the operands are Q10. Nothing in either routine PROVES the operands are Q10; there is no 0x400 constant in either one. The scale is INFERRED from the call sites and is recorded as a scale, not as a fact about the values. THE THIRD FIXED-POINT ROUTINE, 0x03000868, IS NOT IN THIS UNIT AND IS NOT Q10. It has zero `smull`/`smlal`, uses `mla` with `ldrsb` byte loads, and computes in Q18.14 (`lsl #18` with `asr #14` on the same register, 64-bit increment via `adds`/`adc`). Grouping it with these two was this ticket's premise and the measurement refutes it; the committed docs/LIFT_IWRAM_DISPATCH.md already said 18.14, so the brief was the outlier. It remains unlifted and is the recommended next cluster.

ads_match.detail: an ARM Developer Suite 1.2 installation is present on this machine but the licence file it ships licenses a different product, so the ARM compilers cannot be run. No compile has been attempted and no configuration has been tested. The installation is located through ADS12_ROOT.
required_to_unblock: a licensed ADS 1.2 installation, with ADS12_ROOT pointing at it

verdicts_are_independent: SEMANTIC, MODERN_BUILD and ADS_MATCH answer different questions and none is evidence for another. A passing modern build says nothing about the original compiler; a passing semantic run only removes one class of error.

identity.why_not: the original translation unit was built by ARM Developer Suite 1.2 (the surviving command line names tcpp). GCC is a different compiler with a different code generator, so its output cannot establish anything about ADS 1.2.

literal_pools.interpretation: the original's literals are accounted for by the words the unit declares; the modern build pools differently, which is a structural consequence of the compiler rather than a defect in the reconstruction. It is also why a function with a literal load cannot be compared standalone.

comparison.match_claim_note: MEASUREMENT ONLY. This compares a modern GCC build against the cartridge. A modern compiler is not the original compiler, so a difference here is expected and proves nothing; an identity here would also prove nothing about ADS 1.2. ADS_MATCH stays BLOCKED.
